regime_classification.growth: {"dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8% YoY; PMI 56.5","signal_text":"GDP at 7.8% YoY is the headline; GVA is the reality check — and with core sector slipping to 4.8% YoY from 5.0%, the infrastructure backbone of that growth is softening even as PMI Composite holds at 56.5. Capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity and IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY confirm the investment cycle is real, not statistical. The inversion: if services credit is growing at 28.3% YoY while core sector decelerates, this is a services-led expansion with a manufacturing lag — durable only if domestic demand holds through the inflation shock.","badge_label":"Expansion Mode","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.inflation: {"dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 6.09% YoY; Fuel 22.93% YoY","signal_text":"CPI at 6.09% YoY is above the RBI's 6% upper tolerance band for the first time in this cycle, but the composition is what matters: food at 8.94% YoY and fuel at 22.93% YoY are doing the work, while core CPI at 4.5% YoY is rising but not yet alarming. The danger is the second-order chain — fuel at a 95th-percentile print feeds into WPI at 9.92% YoY, which feeds into producer margins, which feeds into core CPI with a two-quarter lag. RBI's own inflation forecast at 5.1% YoY is already stale; the repo rate at 5.25% p.a. implies a real rate of negative 85 bps against headline CPI — the pause is becoming a policy error in slow motion.","badge_label":"Inflation Overshoot","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.credit: {"dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 19.54% YoY; CD ratio 82%","signal_text":"Bank credit at 19.54% YoY against deposit growth at 16.86% YoY — a 268 bps divergence widening for three consecutive months — has pushed the CD ratio to 82%, the 75th percentile of its 10-year range. The last time India sustained a CD ratio above 80% while the repo rate was being held was FY14; within 12 months, external shocks forced an emergency tightening cycle. Today's setup rhymes: NBFC credit growth is already decelerating to 15.4% YoY from 15.8%, the canary in the funding-stress coal mine. Corporates are reading the same signal — ₹1,34,000 cr / month in bond issuance suggests the smart money is bypassing banks before the window narrows.","badge_label":"Deposit Gap Stress","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.policy: {"dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25% p.a.","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% p.a. is unchanged, but the real rate against a 6.09% YoY CPI print is now negative — the RBI is effectively easing into an inflation overshoot. The RBI's own forecast of 5.1% YoY inflation is already below the current print, which means the next MPC meeting will require either a forecast revision or a credibility defence. For housing, the average home loan rate at 7.35% p.a. against an affordability index at 2.3× price-to-income is already stretched; any rate hike to defend the inflation band compresses affordability further and risks a demand cliff in mid-segment residential.","badge_label":"Rate Pause","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.capex: {"dimension":"capex","metric_summary":"IIP CapG 16.9% YoY; CU 77.4% of capacity","signal_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY — the third consecutive month of acceleration — alongside capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (68th percentile) is the most credible signal of a genuine private capex upcycle. The threshold that historically triggers private investment is 80% utilisation; at 77.4%, the economy is close but not there. Manufacturing PMI at 55.7 confirms order books are expanding. The risk: if the CD ratio tightens credit availability and the cost of capital rises, the capex cycle stalls at the threshold — the investment upcycle would be the most expensive near-miss in recent memory.","badge_label":"Capex Upcycle","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.consumption: {"dimension":"consumption","metric_summary":"GST ₹231290 cr/mo; PV 32.1% YoY","signal_text":"GST at ₹2,31,290 cr / month is a 10-year 90th-percentile print, but the composition matters more than the headline — a surge of this magnitude in a single month warrants triangulation against e-way bills and UPI volumes before declaring a demand breakout. Passenger vehicle sales at 32.1% YoY and two-wheeler sales at 33.1% YoY confirm broad-based consumer spending, but the two-wheeler number is the more important signal: it captures the mass-market, semi-urban consumer that GST formalisation can overstate. Commercial vehicle sales at 37.6% YoY — the best proxy for freight and logistics demand — corroborates that this is not purely an urban affluent story.","badge_label":"Demand Surge","badge_type":"b-exp"}

signal_cards.1: {"signal_num":1,"signal_theme":"CREDIT CYCLE","status":"risk","title":"Deposit Gap Forces RBI's Hand","data_text":"Bank credit growth at 19.54% YoY (latest) vs deposit growth at 16.86% YoY — a 268 bps divergence widening for 3 consecutive months (13.8→17.1→19.4→19.54% credit; 10.8→17.8→16.86% deposits). CD ratio at 82% credit-to-deposits, up from 81% last month, now at 75th percentile of 10-year range. NBFC credit growth decelerating to 15.4% YoY from 15.8%, signalling funding stress. Corporate bond issuance at ₹134,000 cr / month suggests corporates are bypassing banks.","implication":"RBI will face pressure to either hike rates (to attract deposits) or relax liquidity conditions by Q2. Banks with CASA ratios below 40% and wholesale funding >30% of liabilities face margin compression. Overweight private banks with CASA >45% (HDFC, Kotak, Axis) — they'll poach deposits. Avoid NBFC exposure with >30% wholesale funding; credit growth will slow sharply if deposit inflows don't accelerate. Watch for RBI's next MPC meeting for forward guidance on rate trajectory.","pct_10y":75,"pct_note":"CD ratio at 75th percentile historically preceded tighter credit conditions and margin pressure on smaller lenders. Last time CD ratio breached 82%, RBI tightened liquidity within 2-3 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.2: {"signal_num":2,"signal_theme":"CAPEX TRIGGER","status":"positive","title":"Capex Upcycle Accelerating, Capacity Tightening","data_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY (latest), up from 16.1% YoY last month — 3rd consecutive month of acceleration. Capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (latest), up from 75.6%, now at 68th percentile of 10-year range. Core sector growth at 4.8% YoY (down from 5% last month) but still supported by steel, cement, and power. Manufacturing PMI at 55.7 index (up from 52.8), signalling strong order books and production expansion.","implication":"Private capex cycle is firmly underway. Overweight capital goods manufacturers (Cummins, Timken, Bharat Electronics), industrial automation (Bosch, ABB), and cement (Ambuja, ACC). Capacity utilisation at 77.4% leaves room for 3-4 quarters of capex before hitting 85%+ constraint. Avoid over-leveraged capex plays; focus on companies with strong balance sheets and order visibility. Public sector capex (railways, roads) will remain steady but private capex is the growth driver.","pct_10y":53,"pct_note":"Capacity utilisation at 77.4% is mid-cycle; historically, sustained capex cycles begin when CU crosses 75% and accelerate until 82-85%. Current trajectory suggests 4-6 quarters of robust capex demand.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.3: {"signal_num":3,"signal_theme":"SIP / RETAIL FLOWS","status":"positive","title":"SIP Inflows Hit 94th Percentile, Retail Conviction Peaks","data_text":"SIP inflows at ₹32,160 cr / month (latest), down marginally from ₹32,490 cr / month but still at 94th percentile of 10-year range. SIP accounts at 10 mn (data quality issue noted, but trend shows sustained participation). SIP AUM at ₹17.68 lakh cr, up from ₹16.64 lakh cr 4 months ago — 6% growth in AUM despite flat account growth suggests ticket size expansion. Equity MF net inflows at ₹32,994 cr / month (down from ₹38,307 cr / month) but still robust. MF AUM at ₹83.39 lakh cr, at 86th percentile of 10-year range.","implication":"Retail equity participation is at cyclical highs. SIP inflows at 94th percentile historically precede market corrections or consolidation phases — not a buy signal, but a signal of late-cycle retail euphoria. Reduce equity allocation; rotate into defensive sectors (FMCG, pharma, utilities). Monitor SIP growth rate (currently 8.9% YoY, down from 15% a year ago) — deceleration will be an early warning of retail fatigue. Debt MF inflows are weak; consider overweighting fixed income for capital preservation.","pct_10y":94,"pct_note":"SIP inflows at 94th percentile have historically coincided with market peaks (2021, early 2024). Retail conviction peaks often precede 10-15% corrections within 3-6 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.4: {"signal_num":4,"signal_theme":"OIL / COMMODITY RISK","status":"risk","title":"Fuel Inflation at 95th Percentile, Import Bill Swelling","data_text":"Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (latest), up from 20.05% YoY last month — 3rd consecutive month of acceleration, now at 95th percentile of 10-year range. WPI at 9.92% YoY (up from 9.78%), driven by fuel and metals. Brent crude at $86.53/bbl (flat), but FAO food index at 136 index (up from 134.5), signalling commodity price stickiness. India's import bill for oil and gas remains elevated; INR depreciation to 92.59 ₹/USD (from 92.9) provides marginal relief but insufficient to offset fuel inflation.","implication":"Fuel inflation will persist through Q2 FY2026 unless Brent falls below $80/bbl. RBI's inflation forecast of 5.1% YoY (up from 4.6%) will constrain rate cuts; expect repo rate to remain at 5.25% p.a. through Q2. Overweight energy stocks (ONGC, Reliance) for dividend yield; avoid consumer discretionary (auto, FMCG) exposed to input cost inflation. Hedge INR depreciation risk — 92.59 is near 10-year highs. Monitor FAO food index; if it breaches 140, headline CPI will spike to 6.5%+.","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"Fuel inflation at 95th percentile historically preceded 6-month periods of sticky headline CPI and RBI rate pause. Last occurrence (2022) led to 200 bps of rate hikes over 6 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.5: {"signal_num":5,"signal_theme":"GLOBAL LIQUIDITY","status":"risk","title":"Fed Tightening Resumes, Carry Trades Unwind","data_text":"Fed funds rate at 3.88% p.a. (up from 3.75% p.a.), rising 3 consecutive months (3.63→3.63→3.75→3.88). US 10Y Treasury yield at 4.92% (down from 5.04%), but Fed balance sheet at $6,741.452 bn (down from $6,753.604 bn) — quantitative tightening continues. US PMI composite at 58.4 index (up from 56), signalling strong US growth. ECB deposit rate at 2.5% p.a. (up from 2.25%), and BOJ rate at 1.25% p.a. (up from 1%), now at 100th percentile of 10-year range. US VIX at 26.62 index (up from 19.3 four months ago), signalling volatility spike.","implication":"Global liquidity is tightening. Carry trades (borrow low in JPY/CHF, invest in INR/emerging markets) are unwinding — expect INR depreciation pressure and FII outflows. FII equity net flows at -₹4,516 cr / month (latest) confirm outflow trend. Reduce EM exposure; overweight India domestic consumption plays insulated from FX volatility. Hedge USD exposure; INR at 92.59 is near 10-year highs. Monitor BOJ rate trajectory — if it reaches 1.5% p.a., carry unwind will accelerate sharply. US 10Y at 4.92% is sticky; expect 4.75-5.25% range through Q2.","pct_10y":62,"pct_note":"Fed tightening at this pace (3 consecutive months) historically preceded 2-3 quarters of EM currency weakness and FII outflows. BOJ at 100th percentile is a structural shift in carry dynamics.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.6: {"signal_num":6,"signal_theme":"INR / FX RESERVES","status":"watch","title":"INR Holds 92.59, But Carry Unwind Looms","data_text":"INR at 92.59 ₹/USD (down from 92.9), now at 85th percentile of 10-year range — near 10-year highs. DXY at 104.336 index (flat), but US VIX at 26.62 (up from 19.3 four months ago) signals risk-off sentiment. FII equity net flows at -₹4,516 cr / month (latest), reversing from +₹29,631 cr / month three months ago. DII equity net flows at ₹6,222 cr / month (down from ₹51,829 cr / month), suggesting domestic support is weakening. India's current account deficit remains manageable, but FX reserve adequacy (import cover ~10 months) is adequate but not excessive.","implication":"INR is holding due to RBI intervention and domestic demand, but carry unwind from BOJ/ECB tightening will pressure it to 93.50-94.50 ₹/USD by Q2. FII outflows will accelerate if US 10Y yields stay above 5%. Corporates should hedge USD exposure; importers benefit from INR weakness but exporters face headwinds. RBI will likely intervene to prevent INR from breaching 94, but reserves will deplete if outflows persist. Monitor FII flows weekly — if they turn negative for 2 consecutive weeks, expect RBI to tighten liquidity or signal rate hikes.","pct_10y":85,"pct_note":"INR at 85th percentile of 10-year range historically preceded 2-3 quarters of depreciation pressure. Last time INR was this strong (2021), it weakened 8% over 6 months as carry trades unwound.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.7: {"signal_num":7,"signal_theme":"UNDER THE RADAR","status":"surprise","title":"Office Absorption Collapsed, But Rents Sticky — GCC Shift Underway","data_text":"Office absorption at 4.02 mn sq ft / quarter (latest), down 73% from 14.1 mn sq ft / quarter four months ago — a cliff-edge decline now at 0th percentile of 10-year range. Yet office vacancy at 13.4% (down from 14.5%), and rents in Bengaluru at ₹103.6 / sqft / month and Mumbai at ₹156 / sqft / month remain sticky despite absorption collapse. Nifty IT index flat while office absorption craters. Retail mall vacancy at 11.15% (down from 11.6%), suggesting e-commerce GMV growth at 25% YoY is NOT cannibalizing physical retail. Airline passenger traffic at 8.64 mn / month (data anomaly, but trend shows volatility).","implication":"Traditional IT services (TCS, Infosys, Wipro) are NOT the marginal office tenant anymore. Global Capability Centers (GCCs) — captive R&D centers of tech giants (Google, Microsoft, Apple, Amazon) — are the new office occupiers. They're selective, high-quality tenants with long-term leases, explaining sticky rents despite low absorption. This decouples commercial RE from IT services stock performance. Overweight commercial RE REITs (Embassy, Mindspace) on GCC demand tailwind, NOT on IT services growth. Underweight traditional IT services on office space headwinds — they're consolidating footprints. Retail mall vacancy decline despite e-commerce surge suggests omnichannel retail (D2C brands, quick-commerce hubs) is the growth driver, not traditional retail.","pct_10y":0,"pct_note":"Office absorption at 0th percentile is unprecedented in 10-year data, yet rents remain sticky — this inversion signals a structural shift in tenant mix from IT services to GCCs. Last time absorption collapsed this sharply (2020 COVID), rents fell 15-20% within 2 quarters; the fact that rents are holding suggests GCC demand is offsetting IT services decline.","is_surprise":true}

executive_summary.1:
{"para_num":1,"para_label":"India Macro Regime","para_html":"

7.8% GDP Headline, 4.8% Core Sector — Services Carrying a Manufacturing Lag

The facts:

  • India GDP at 7.8% YoY, PMI Composite at 56.5, and IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY — three expansion signals in alignment.
  • But core sector growth slipped to 4.8% YoY from 5.0%, and services credit at 28.3% YoY is doing the heavy lifting that manufacturing has not yet matched.
  • GST at ₹2,31,290 cr / month (90th percentile) is the strongest demand proxy — but a single-month surge of this magnitude requires e-way bill corroboration before it reads as a structural demand breakout.
  • Capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity is 250 bps below the ~80% threshold that historically triggers private capex commitment.

The tension: The headline growth complex is unambiguously strong; the sub-surface tells a more conditional story — services-led, credit-fuelled, and 250 bps short of the utilisation level that converts intention into private investment.

Bottom line: Watch e-way bill volumes for the GST corroboration; if they confirm, upgrade consumption conviction — if they lag, the ₹2,31,290 cr / month print is formalisation, not demand.

"}
executive_summary.2:
{"para_num":2,"para_label":"Global Macro Regime","para_html":"

US Re-Acceleration Meets BOJ at 100th Percentile — Carry Unwind Is the Underpriced Tail

The facts:

  • US GDP SAAR accelerated to 3.4% SAAR from 2.2%, and US PMI Composite at 58.4 (80th percentile) signals the Fed has no near-term cover to pause.
  • BOJ rate at 1.25% p.a. — 100th percentile of its 10-year range, rising for the second consecutive meeting — is unwinding the yen carry trade that funded EM positioning for a decade.
  • US VIX at 26.62, up from 19.3 four months ago, and S&P 500 falling for five consecutive sessions to 6,910 suggest the re-acceleration narrative is not being believed by equity markets.
  • But Eurozone GDP at 0.4% YoY with CPI at 4.0% YoY — stagflation arithmetic — limits ECB's ability to ease and removes a global growth buffer.

The tension: DM survey data signals re-acceleration; DM equity markets are pricing deceleration. The BOJ at a 10-year extreme is the mechanism that resolves the contradiction — yen carry unwind tightens global financial conditions regardless of what the Fed does.

Bottom line: BOJ at 1.25% p.a. is the single most underappreciated risk to India's FII flows; watch the yen cross — any move through 140 ¥/USD accelerates EM outflows.

"}
executive_summary.3:
{"para_num":3,"para_label":"Liquidity Conditions","para_html":"

SIP Autopilot Holds, But DII Absorption Collapsing — Domestic Backstop Is Thinning

The facts:

  • SIP inflows at ₹32,160 cr / month (94th percentile) remain structurally anchored, with SIP AUM at ₹17.68 lakh cr — ticket-size expansion compensating for flat account growth.
  • But DII equity net flows collapsed to ₹6,222 cr / month from ₹51,829 cr / month — the domestic institutional backstop that absorbed FII selling has largely withdrawn.
  • FII equity net at -₹4,516 cr / month, reversing from +₹29,631 cr / month three months ago — the direction of travel is clear even if the quantum is not yet alarming.
  • MF AUM at ₹83.39 lakh cr (86th percentile) provides a structural floor, but equity MF net inflows fell to ₹32,994 cr / month from ₹38,307 cr / month.

The tension: Retail SIP flows are holding; institutional flows — both FII and DII — are retreating simultaneously. SIP inflows alone cannot absorb a sustained FII exit if the BOJ carry unwind accelerates.

Bottom line: If DII equity net flows fall below ₹3,000 cr / month for a second consecutive month, the market loses its domestic absorption buffer — watch this number before adding equity exposure.

"}
executive_summary.4:
{"para_num":4,"para_label":"Equity + Real Estate Implications","para_html":"

Bank Nifty at 100th Percentile, REITs Down 20–30% — Two Markets, One Economy

The facts:

  • NRI residential buying is FALLING — NRI share at 18% of purchases (prior 15%, but directionally declining), with NRI share within premium/luxury at 32%; remittances at $155.1 bn (14.5% YoY) provide macro support but are not translating into incremental property demand.
  • Hyderabad leads residential momentum — sales +15% YoY, launches +120% YoY, unsold inventory at 28 months — while NCR sales are -1% YoY and Chennai -10% YoY; the market is bifurcating sharply by city.
  • Office absorption at 4.02 mn sq ft / quarter (0th percentile) has collapsed 73% from 14.1 mn sq ft / quarter, yet Embassy REIT at ₹370/unit and Mindspace at ₹345/unit are down 12–31% from prior levels — the market is pricing the absorption cliff.
  • Bank Nifty at 62,585 (100th percentile) is pricing a banking system that the CD ratio at 82% and decelerating NBFC credit growth at 15.4% YoY do not fully support.

The tension: Equities are pricing banking strength and consumption momentum; real estate and REIT markets are pricing credit tightening and occupier retreat. Both cannot be right simultaneously.

Bottom line: Avoid office REITs until GCC absorption data for Q4 2026 confirms whether the 73% quarterly collapse is a one-quarter anomaly or a structural demand reset.

"}
executive_summary.5:
{"para_num":5,"para_label":"Key Risks to Monitor","para_html":"

Three Fuses, One Detonator — Sequence Matters

The facts:

  • Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile, rising three consecutive months) feeding into WPI at 9.92% YoY — if Brent breaks above $90/bbl, the RBI's pause becomes untenable and a rate hike re-enters the probability distribution.
  • BOJ at 1.25% p.a. (100th percentile) — every 25 bps BOJ hike historically triggers yen carry unwind, pressuring EM currencies; INR at 92.59 ₹/USD (85th percentile) has limited buffer before imported inflation compounds the fuel shock.
  • CD ratio at 82% with credit growing at 19.54% YoY and NBFC credit decelerating to 15.4% YoY — if deposit growth slips below 15% YoY, macro-prudential tightening via risk weights becomes the RBI's next move, not a rate cut.
  • S&P 500 falling five consecutive sessions to 6,910 with US VIX at 26.62 — a sustained DM equity correction would accelerate FII outflows from India beyond the current -₹4,516 cr / month run-rate.

The tension: Each risk is manageable in isolation; the danger is sequencing — a BOJ hike triggers INR weakness, which amplifies fuel inflation, which forces RBI tightening, which stresses the CD ratio. The chain is short.

Bottom line: Watch Brent crude this week: a close above $90/bbl resets the RBI rate-cut narrative to rate-hike risk and is the single most consequential data point for India macro positioning.

"}
